thread:
alex: noticing strange client loop on canary. users hitting a 503 -> reconnect -> immediate rate-limit -> reconnect again. console shows two different trace_ids for same session :confused:
dev-bot: ERROR at proxy-2: session handoff failed, auth mismatch, resume_token invalidated by route-swap (logs: 
  proxy/handshake.go:142: resume validation failed: token_ns != route_ns
  conn: 0x7f8a3b
)
maria: Ugh. Are we sure this is a resume token namespace leak and not the client dropping cookies? Any correlation id? :eyes:
alex: trace_ids in console are different but requestids (X-Req-Id) match. looks like server accepted a reconnect on old route, then client got a 429 and retried to a different region which accepted, creating two sessions. Console shows duplicate billing events for ~30s window.
priya: can you paste the minimal repro curl? also which quota bucket is being hit?
alex: curl --http2 -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://stream.redwood.test/v1/stream?resume=abc123"
  headers show `x-route: r-east-1` then later `x-route: r-west-2` after a retry. quota bucket is "streaming_active_sessions" at 250/s.
sam: that bucket is global but we do per-route accounting. race when route swap happens + delayed quorum update -> double-count. Ops SRE?
ops-sre: confirmed: meter shows short-lived double increments when resume accepted on old proxy then fallback to new. telemetry tag `route_version` missing on the second accept so console groups them separately.
maria: fix options: (1) server-side single-writer fence on resume_token (reject if token.ns != current_ns) + return `retry-after` with consistent trace id, (2) short grace window that absorbs duplicate increments, (3) console change to join events by X-Req-Id when duplicate trace ids differ.
priya: (1) seems safest for correctness but could break legitimate cross-region failover. we need to allow controlled failover for dedicated customers. maybe only enforce fence when `route_version` mismatch and `auth_ttl < 5s`?
sam: what about adding a quick metric `resume_detach` and tagging with `session_key` so graphs can show the spike pattern instead of billing misattribution? low-risk and helps diagnosis.
alex: can we ship (3) console-side grouping quick fix first? low-risk. follow with (1) as opt-in server flag behind `feature.resume_fence` for canary.
priya: agree. I'll sketch telemetry tags: `session_key`, `resume_epoch`, `route_ns`, `route_version`, and `xreqid`. Console team needs to map `xreqid` as primary join key for streaming billing.
maria: I'll own the server flag rollout; put it behind canary and a kill switch. add a short TTL for allowed cross-route acceptance (5s) to not block steady cross-region migration.
ops-sre: deploying a probe to canary tomorrow that simulates resume->route-swap races. will add dashboard panel for `resume_detach` and a graph for duplicate billing counts.
alex: created a quick follow-up ticket in /eng-platform backlog. minimal unit tests and an integration test with two proxies. tagging @maria @priya for review. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: deploy job queued: deploy/canary/resume-fence-feature flag -> pending checks
priya: leaving notes here: need to update docs about resume semantics and console join key. also add an alert when `duplicate_billing_rate > 0.5%` of sessions for 1m.
alex: thanks all, we'll monitor metrics and rollback if anything spikes.
